title: Top Local Payment Methods in Thailand: How Thais Pay
summary: From PromptPay QR and mobile banking to TrueMoney and cards, see how Thais pay online and in store, and how to accept every method with one integration. The post Top Local Payment Methods in Thailand: How Thais Pay appeared first on Xendit .
body_markdown:
In Thailand, the default way to pay is straight from a bank account. Shoppers scan a PromptPay QR code or approve the payment in their bank app, online and in store. Wallets, cards and direct debit cover what bank payments leave open: everyday wallet spending, international buyers, installment purchases and subscriptions. This guide covers the six payment methods in Thailand that matter most, who uses each one, and when to offer it. Each section links to our in-depth guide for that category.


**Key takeaways**


- Account-to-account payments, mostly PromptPay and mobile banking, made up 44% of e-commerce value and 43% of point-of-sale value in Thailand in 2025.


- PromptPay QR belongs on every checkout. PromptPay processed 2.38 billion transactions worth THB 4.70 trillion in December 2025 alone.


- TrueMoney and ShopeePay are the wallets Thai consumers say they prefer. WeChat Pay matters if you serve visitors from China.


- Cards remain essential for travel, subscriptions and international buyers, and Thai banks offer card installments on large purchases.


- Saved cards and direct debit handle recurring billing. Virtual accounts handle B2B invoices.


- With Xendit, you can accept 100+ payment methods through one integration.


## **How Thais pay today**


Thailand has one of the most advanced real-time payment markets in the world, and it shows at checkout. Account-to-account payments, mostly PromptPay and mobile banking, made up 44% of e-commerce value and 43% of point-of-sale value in 2025, the highest share of any Southeast Asian market (


[Fintech News Singapore, citing the Global Payments Report 2026](https://fintechnews.sg/128337/e-commerce/southeast-asia-payment-methods-2026-global-payments-report/) ).


PromptPay, the national real-time payment system, sits at the centre of it all. It had more than 82.21 million registrations by December 2025 and processed 2.38 billion transactions worth THB 4.70 trillion in that month alone. Thais now make more than 300 real-time payments per person each year, putting Thailand third in the world for real-time payment use (


[Mastercard, with National ITMX](https://www.mastercard.com/global/en/news-and-trends/Insights/2026/real-time-payments-ignite-thailand-as-an-economic-force.html) ).


Wallets and cards still matter. TrueMoney and ShopeePay are the wallets Thais say they prefer, cards remain important for bigger purchases and international shoppers, and cash on delivery is still common, with Thailand’s COD share among the highest in the world (Fintech News Singapore, same source).


This guide walks through the six payment method categories that matter most, who uses each one, and when to offer it. Each section links to our in-depth guide for that category.

## **1. PromptPay QR: Thailand’s default way to pay**


PromptPay is Thailand’s national real-time payment system, launched under the Bank of Thailand and operated by National ITMX. Thai QR, the national QR standard built on top of it, lets a customer pay any merchant by scanning one code with any Thai bank app or supported e-wallet.


The scale is hard to overstate. PromptPay handled peak days of more than 80 million transactions in 2025, and almost 400,000 businesses were registered to receive payments on it (


[Mastercard, with National ITMX](https://www.mastercard.com/global/en/news-and-trends/Insights/2026/real-time-payments-ignite-thailand-as-an-economic-force.html) ). PromptPay QR is also linked with neighbouring QR systems, including Malaysia’s DuitNow, so some tourists can pay with their home banking apps (


[PayNet](https://www.paynet.my/about-us/media-centre/press-release/8-44-billion-transactions-processed-in-2025-as-digital-payments-become-malaysians-preferred-way-to-pay.html) ).


How it works: the merchant shows a PromptPay QR code at the counter, on a checkout page or in a payment link. On desktop, the customer scans it with their phone; on mobile, they save the QR image and open it from their bank app. They check the amount and merchant, then confirm.


When to offer it: always. PromptPay QR is the one method nearly every Thai shopper can use, from street food to online electronics. With Xendit, PromptPay QR supports payments from THB 1 to THB 700,000, works with payment links, and settles instantly.

## **2. Mobile banking: pay straight from the bank app**


Mobile banking apps are part of daily life in Thailand, and many shoppers prefer to approve online payments there rather than type in card details. Mobile banking checkout sends the customer to their own bank app to approve the payment in a few taps.


How it works: the customer chooses their bank at checkout and is redirected to the bank app (for example K PLUS or SCB EASY). They review the amount, confirm with a PIN or biometrics, and are returned to the merchant with instant confirmation.


When to offer it: for online checkout on mobile, especially higher-value orders such as electronics, travel, insurance and education fees. With Xendit, you can accept mobile banking payments from Kasikornbank, Siam Commercial Bank, Bangkok Bank, Krungthai Bank and Krungsri, from THB 20 to THB 700,000 per transaction.

## 3. E-wallets: everyday spending and tourists


E-wallets are a smaller slice of checkout in Thailand than PromptPay and mobile banking, but they are central to everyday spending, promotions and super-app ecosystems. TrueMoney and ShopeePay are the wallets Thai consumers say they prefer (


[Fintech News Singapore, citing GPR 2026](https://fintechnews.sg/128337/e-commerce/southeast-asia-payment-methods-2026-global-payments-report/) ).


The wallets that matter most:


- TrueMoney Wallet: the broadest-reach wallet in Thailand, used for shopping, bills, mobile top-ups and online services.


- ShopeePay: the go-to wallet for Shopee shoppers and promo-driven online purchases.


- LINE Pay: built into LINE, one of Thailand’s most used messaging apps, which makes it a natural fit for social commerce.


- WeChat Pay: how many visitors from China prefer to pay, important for hotels, retail and tourist attractions.


How it works: the customer picks a wallet at checkout, is redirected to the app, and confirms. Payment is confirmed instantly.


When to offer it: for consumer-facing businesses such as F&B, fashion, gaming and digital goods, and for tourism businesses serving Chinese visitors. With Xendit, you can accept TrueMoney, ShopeePay, LINE Pay and WeChat Pay.


***Read also:***[E-Wallets in Thailand: A Complete Guide for Businesses Accepting Digital Payments](https://www.xendit.co/en-th/blog/e-wallets-in-thailand-a-complete-guide-for-businesses-accepting-digital-payments/)


## **4. Credit and debit cards, with instalments**


Cards are no longer the first choice for most Thai shoppers, but they remain essential for travel bookings, subscriptions, larger purchases and customers from abroad. Instalments are a big part of the card story in Thailand: many cardholders expect to split a large purchase into monthly payments with their bank, often interest-free.


How it works: the customer enters card details at checkout and usually completes a 3D Secure check with their bank. They can pay in full, choose an instalment plan from their card-issuing bank, or save the card for one-click and recurring billing.


When to offer it: for SaaS and subscriptions, travel and hospitality, premium retail, electronics, and any business with foreign customers. With Xendit, you can accept Visa, Mastercard, JCB, UnionPay and American Express, charge saved cards for recurring payments, and offer card instalments from Bangkok Bank, Kasikornbank, Krungsri, Krungthai, SCB, TTB, and KTC on purchases from THB 3,000 to THB 700,000.

## 5. Direct debit: set it and forget it


Direct debit lets a customer link their bank account to your business once and authorise future charges, so they do not have to approve every payment. It is the bank-account alternative to saving a card.


How it works: the customer chooses their bank, logs in to authorise the link, and confirms the first payment. After that, you can charge the account on a schedule or on demand, within what the customer has agreed to.


When to offer it: for subscriptions, memberships, insurance premiums, loan repayments and utilities. With Xendit, you can accept direct debit from Bangkok Bank, Krungsri, Krungthai Bank and SCB, all supporting recurring and merchant-initiated charges.


***Read also:***[How Credit Card Payments Work in Thailand: A Guide for Businesses](https://www.xendit.co/en-th/blog/how-credit-card-payments-work-in-thailand-a-guide-for-businesses/)


## **6. Bank transfer via virtual account: for invoices and B2B**


For businesses that collect by bank transfer, a virtual account gives each customer or invoice its own account number. Every payment lands against that number, so it matches the right invoice automatically, with no transfer slips to chase.


How it works: the customer receives an account number and transfers to it from any Thai bank. The payment is identified and confirmed as soon as it arrives.


When to offer it: for B2B invoicing, wholesale, tuition, and other payments where customers are used to paying by transfer. With Xendit, you can collect into a Standard Chartered virtual account from THB 20 to THB 700,000 per transaction.


***Read also:***[Virtual Account Payments in Thailand: A Business Guide to Smarter Bank Transfer Collection](https://www.xendit.co/en-th/blog/virtual-account-payments-in-thailand-a-business-guide-to-smarter-bank-transfer-collection/)


## **How to choose the right payment mix**


There is no single best method; the right mix depends on what you sell, your average order value, and whether customers pay once or repeatedly. As a baseline, PromptPay QR plus mobile banking reaches almost every Thai shopper, and cards add the higher-value and international customers.

A few practical rules help whichever mix you choose. Put PromptPay QR first on every checkout. On mobile, make it easy to save or open the QR in a bank app, or offer mobile banking so the customer does not have to leave the device. Track success and drop-off rates per method, then add or reorder options based on what your own customers use.

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)


**What is the most popular payment method in Thailand?**


Account-to-account payments, led by PromptPay and mobile banking, are the largest method both online and in store, at 44% of e-commerce value and 43% of point-of-sale value in 2025.


**What is the difference between PromptPay and Thai QR?**


PromptPay is the national real-time payment system that moves money between accounts. Thai QR is the standard QR code format that lets customers pay a merchant through PromptPay by scanning one code with any bank app.


**Which e-wallets should I accept in Thailand?**


TrueMoney has the broadest reach, ShopeePay suits online shoppers, and LINE Pay fits social commerce. Add WeChat Pay if you serve tourists from China.


**Can Thai customers pay in instalments without a credit card?**


Instalment plans in Thailand are mostly offered through credit cards, which Xendit supports with seven banks and card issuers. Customers without a credit card usually pay in full with PromptPay QR or mobile banking.


**Which methods support recurring payments?**


Saved cards and direct debit from Bangkok Bank, Krungsri, Krungthai Bank and SCB can be charged again after the customer’s first authorisation, which makes them the best fit for subscriptions.
